[April 2016]

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu locks the door to his office. He turns to see President Reuven Rivlin and Yossi Cohen, Director of Mossad, sitting in two identical grand antique chairs in front of his large desk. He pours himself a drink - straight whiskey - before he ushers the first word in the conversation.

"Our people once again face an uncertain future, one where we are at the mercy of those who despise our very existence. A scotch if I remember correctly, Reuven?"

"Thank you Ben". "And for you, Yossi?" "Gin - hold the tonic".

 

Netanyahu walks over to his desk, hands the men their drinks and takes his seat in front of a pair of Star of David and American flags. Director Cohen has a suggestion,

"On my recent visit to The States I had an interesting meeting with Michael Rogers. It seems that while the surveillance of their citizens produces data faster than it can be analysed, they are capable of analysing data for several hundred thousand individuals in real time. Now my suggestion is not to do a similar program here, but rather analyse individuals for certain unfavourable characteristics and keep a record of such people. Supposing a weeks worth of surveillance is enough to reasonably determine someone's allegiances, at a rate of 10000 people at a time, such a list could be complete in at most 16 years, and an incomplete list could be made in just a year."

 

President Rivlin is slightly disturbed by this possibility, and question the expense of such an operation, while Netanyahu stares at his whiskey glass, deep in thought. Cohen continues,

"If we wanted to determine people likely to commit acts of terrorism, something that requires specialist algorithms and manpower for surveillance, the expense would be in the order of billions and would require more agents than I have (Mossad only has around 1200 employees). However, if we want to know the identities of radical feminists for example, that list would take very little time, money and at most a handful of employees, such people tend to be active on social media so would be easy to identify with a keyword search. Also -"

Netanyahu interupts, "how feasible would it be to construct lists of socialists, politically active leftists, religious Muslims, atheists and two state activists?". "An increase in my budget of US$1 billion, and I can have a slightly inaccurate database ready within the year, but you must know that list could be even a million names in length."

"Oy vey!" Rivlin utters, clearly uncomfortable with the idea.

"Get it done." Netanyahu thanks Cohen as he leaves the room.

 

"What are you planning to do with this Ben?" Rivlin asks, hoping for some reassurance. "I am not completely certain yet. But I am certain that before you can defeat your enemy, you need to know their name."

tl;dr - Mossad is going to construct a database to contain the identities of socialists, religious Muslims, atheists, politically active leftists and two-state solution campaigners. The operation will take a year to complete, costing about US$1 billion, but will be slightly inaccurate. Oy vey!
